supportTiers.Full: A packed-NuGet consumer publishes and executes as Native AOT without TCJ-caused trimming or AOT warnings for the supported usage path.
supportTiers.Conditional: The package is supported only through explicitly documented safe paths or while respecting named upstream restrictions.
supportTiers.Experimental: The package may be exercised with Native AOT, but TCJ does not make a production-support promise for that path.
supportTiers.Unsupported: TCJ does not support Native AOT consumption for the package or usage path.

packages.rationale: TCJ.Core is library-level Native AOT and trimming compatible: its production project declares IsAotCompatible=true and the packed-package Core.Console consumer builds with the SDK AOT/trim analyzers enabled. The repository support tier remains Conditional until the packed Native AOT publish-and-execute evidence required for a formal Full support claim is introduced by Important 8.
Framework-service registration can be used without scanning application assemblies, but convention registration performs runtime reflection over supplied assemblies.

restrictions.reason: Supplying one or more assemblies invokes Assembly.GetTypes()-based convention scanning. Native AOT callers must not rely on this reflection-discovery path unless the application independently preserves every discovered type.
The overload is AOT-safe only while the configured assembly scan set remains empty. Adding assemblies selects the reflection-discovery path.
The overload is AOT-safe only while TcjDependencyInjectionOptions.Assemblies is empty; populated scan sets are enumerated through runtime reflection.
These APIs opt the caller into convention scanning and therefore into the reflection-based path described by this policy.

packages.rationale: EF Core NativeAOT support remains upstream-experimental and TCJ also exposes reflection-driven model-discovery and entity-search paths.

restrictions.reason: The upstream EF Core NativeAOT feature is documented as experimental, may emit trimming/AOT warnings, does not support dynamic queries, and has additional query/provider limitations.
The API discovers configuration types with reflection and invokes closed generic ApplyConfiguration methods dynamically.
The API discovers entity types with Assembly.GetExportedTypes() at runtime.
The search path constructs closed generic executor types dynamically from EF model metadata.
Resolving an unregistered convention event name falls back to scanning loaded assemblies. Native AOT consumers must explicitly register persisted event contracts with AddTcjOutboxEvent<TEvent>.

packages.rationale: The package inherits the upstream experimental EF Core NativeAOT contract and cannot be promoted beyond that upstream boundary without packaged-consumer evidence for the provider path.

restrictions.symbol: Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore NativeAOT and precompiled queries / provider support
restrictions.reason: EF Core NativeAOT is upstream-experimental, and EF providers participate in precompiled-query support; TCJ therefore makes no Full production-support claim for the SQL Server path.

packages.rationale: ASP.NET Core supports Native AOT only for a defined subset of framework features, so TCJ.AspNetCore support is bounded by the application's selected ASP.NET Core feature set and future packaged-consumer evidence.

restrictions.symbol: ASP.NET Core Native AOT feature compatibility matrix for net10.0
restrictions.reason: Native AOT support varies by ASP.NET Core feature; for example Minimal APIs are only partially supported while MVC, Blazor Server, and SignalR are not supported. TCJ.AspNetCore is supported only inside upstream-supported application paths.
